title: Sales order to production order
content: A sales order records customer demand. A production order converts confirmed demand into a manufacturing execution plan. In an ERP-MES integration, the ERP system usually owns customer demand, pricing, and delivery commitment, while MES owns shop-floor execution, reporting, and exception feedback.

title: BOM version change handling
content: When a BOM version changes, the team should confirm the effective date, affected sales orders, open production orders, and existing inventory. If a work order has already started, the system should avoid silent replacement and create an exception review task.

title: Inventory inconsistency between WMS and MES
content: If WMS inventory differs from MES material consumption, the assistant should ask for material code, warehouse, batch number, work order, and transaction time. Typical causes include delayed posting, manual adjustment, barcode scanning error, or cross-warehouse transfer not synchronized.

title: Quality inspection exception escalation
content: When inspection fails, the system should record defect category, defect quantity, responsible process, inspector, photos if available, and disposition decision. The next step may be rework, concession release, scrap, or supplier claim.

title: Manufacturing gross margin analysis
content: Manufacturing gross margin analysis should compare sales revenue, material cost, labor cost, manufacturing overhead, outsourcing cost, and abnormal loss. The assistant should separate order-level margin from product-line margin and highlight data source assumptions.
